mechanics: Infernal Cry gem has two parts: Infernal Cry and Combust. These are distinct skills and do not share all their stats. Both the explosion and Combust can be affected by support gems linked to Infernal Cry.

wikiContext.title: Shrine
wikiContext.summary: Shrines are special objects that apply an effect to nearby monsters or cast spells at nearby players. Interacting them allows the player to temporarily steal their power for themselves. This mechanic is also referred to as Domination.
mechanics: Shrines can appear randomly in most areas. Shrines are often surrounded by a pack of monsters guarding it. Initially, shrines will only buff enemies and damage players. When touched, the shrine's effect is removed and given to the player for 45 seconds (20 seconds for Divine Shrines) in the form of a status effect. Shrine effects will either buff the player (but not their allies) or cast spells that damage enemies. A player can be affected by multiple different shrine effects.
Shrine effect duration and buff effect can be modified with certain items and passives.

mechanics: The gem consists of two components: a skill part Arcanist Brand and a support part Arcanist Brand Support. It does not however have the Support gem tag. It is one of the few skill/support hybrid gems.

Arcanist Brand: * Increases and Reductions to Cast Speed also apply to this Skill's Activation frequency ** Arcanist Brand's cast speed determines how long it takes to cast the brand itself. The activation frequency is how often the brand triggers linked spells. Both of these are increased by cast speed modifiers. More/less modifiers (e.g. Spell Echo Support) and modifiers to action speed will only affect the brand's cast time, and not its activation frequency.

Modifiers to your Wither effect will affect the reflected Wither. It is recommended to have some protection or prevention against chaos damage, such as Chaos Inoculation or .

wikiContext.title: Aspect of Lunaris
wikiContext.summary: Aspect of Lunaris is a Pantheon aspect skill that grants a buff which grants Lunar Protection or Lunar Resistance stacks on taking physical or elemental damage respectively, stackable buffs which lessen physical or elemental damage. Only one aspect skill can be active at a time.
mechanics: Lunar Protection causes you to take 2% less physical damage per stack; Lunar Resistance causes you to take 2% less elemental damage per stack. These two buffs are independent. These buffs can each stack up to 8 times, up to 16% less physical and elemental damage taken respectively. Gaining a stack will refresh its duration.
Self-damage (e.g. Boneshatter, Enmity's Embrace) can proc these stacks consistently without requiring an enemy to hit you.

wikiContext.title: Aspect of Solaris
wikiContext.summary: Aspect of Solaris is a Pantheon aspect skill that grants a buff which inflicts Fire exposure on enemies within its radius, and periodically inflicts the stackable Sunscald debuff which increases the effect of exposure on affected enemies. Only one aspect skill can be active at a time.
mechanics: This buff inflicts a base exposure effect of -10% to fire resistance.

The Sunscald debuff has a base duration of 4 seconds and stacks up to 5 times, with each stack increasing exposure effect by 15%, or a total of 75% increased exposure effect on affected enemies. It is inflicted once every second; the interval cannot be modified. It affects all types of exposure applied by any skill or effect, not just the fire exposure from the skill.

wikiContext.title: Aspect of the Avian

The first buff grants you and your minions chance to deal double damage, and the second buff grants increased movement speed to you and your minions. Only one aspect skill can be active at a time.
mechanics: The game will track the time remaining for each buff and resume counting upon reactivation (for example, you cannot rapidly toggle the skill, remove/re-equip the gem, or cycle equipment to spend more time in one buff than allotted).

The game will track the time remaining for each buff and resume counting upon reactivation (for example, you cannot rapidly toggle the skill, remove/re-equip the gem, or cycle equipment to spend more time in one buff than allotted).

wikiContext.title: Autoexertion
wikiContext.summary: Autoexertion is a skill gem that reserves mana for each supported warcry skill to have them trigger automatically once off cooldown. Supported warcries no longer grant buffs or charges, but can still exert attacks and debuff enemies.
mechanics: When linked to Autoexertion, all supported warcries each have a base reservation of 20%. This reservation is modified by support gems and modifiers to reservation efficiency. These modified reservations are then added together, and the sum is used as a single reservation for the Autoexertion skill itself, which cannot be further modified. Prism Guardian and Blood Magic can be used to reserve life instead of mana. Arrogance Support will also allow this, but the reservation multiplier will apply.
Autoexertion does not cause warcries to share a cooldown; each warcry will automatically trigger at the end of their cooldowns.

For example, it can be used to automate Steelskin, Withering Step, and Detonate Mines all at once.

wikiContext.summary: Sacrifice of Blood is a keystone passive skill/keyword which causes life regeneration while at full life to give the user a Blood Barrier that can absorb damage from incoming hits, at the cost of halving the user's life regeneration rate.
mechanics: Sacrifice of Blood will only grant a Blood Barrier while the conditions for full life is active. Any life reservation or mechanics preventing life from recovering to full such as Petrified Blood will block it. The You count as on Full Life while at 90% of maximum Life or above Life Mastery will grant Blood Barrier while you have at least 90% life, and Coward's Chains will cause you to always gain Blood Barrier.

Blood Barrier is granted based on tooltip life regeneration including modifiers to life regeneration rate; modifiers to life recovery rate does not affect Blood Barrier gain. The actual life recovered per second is not considered and the rate of gain is not affected by any ongoing damage over time or life loss over time effects (as long as you're on full life). This allows Sacrifice of Blood to be used with effects that prevent recovery from life regeneration like Vaal Pact.

mechanics: Shrines can appear randomly in most areas. Shrines are often surrounded by a pack of monsters guarding it. Initially, shrines will only buff enemies and damage players. Shrine effects will either buff the player (but not their allies) or cast spells that damage enemies. A player can be affected by multiple different shrine effects.
Shrine effect duration and buff effect can be modified with certain items and passives.

wikiContext.title: Burning
wikiContext.summary: Burning refers to any fire damage over time effect. Burning damage is a synonym for fire damage over time; all burning damage is fire damage over time, and vice versa.
mechanics: There are several sources of burning, for example: * Ignite * Burning ground (Fire Trap, Flame Dash, etc.) * Righteous Fire * Searing Bond * Scorching Ray * Herald of Ash

Different sources of burning damage stack cumulatively, but multiple applications from the same source do not. For example, two Spell Totem linked with Righteous Fire will not double the burn damage, however a Spell Totem linked with Righteous Fire together with a Searing Bond totem will stack with each other. Stacking rules for buffs, debuffs or other effects are defined in terms of that specific buff, debuff or effect interacting with other applications of the same effect, not with other ones that are similar.

wikiContext.title: Aspect of the Cat
wikiContext.summary: Aspect of the Cat is an aspect skill that grants two alternating buffs, each with their own duration. Cat's Stealth increases the character's stealth, gives a chance to avoid all damage from hits, and increases critical strike chance. Cat's Agility increases attack and cast speed. By default, their durations are 4 and 6 seconds respectively. Only one aspect skill can be active at a time.
mechanics: If crafting the Aspect of the Cat on gear that has sockets, or the Aspect skill from Farrul's Bite, the skill can be supported by socketed support gems. For example, More Duration Support, Less Duration Support or Efficacy Support to alter the buff duration of Cat's Stealth and Cat's Agility. Or supported by Arrogance Support to reserve life instead of mana.

The game will track the time remaining for each buff and resume counting upon reactivation (for example, you cannot rapidly toggle the skill, remove/re-equip the gem, or cycle equipment to spend more time in one buff than allotted).

wikiContext.title: Chill
wikiContext.summary: Chill is an elemental ailment inherent to cold that applies a slow effect to the character, reducing the animation speed at which the character plays. __TOC__
mechanics: A hit of cold damage will attempt to inflict chill. This will occur regardless of whether or not the hit critically strikes. By default, only cold damage is able to inflict chill. Some skill effects and modifiers, such as Chilled ground and Summon Skitterbots, apply chill without dealing damage.

The base duration of chill is 2 seconds and its effect is determined based on the the amount of Cold damage dealt relative to the enemy's ailment threshold. When inflicted through non-damage means, its base effect is 10%. Chill's effect is capped at 30% reduced action speed. The Elementalist's Shaper of Winter passive increases this up to 40%. Chill's minimum effect is 5%; any chill of lesser effect than that is discarded. The effect of chill is calculated using the following formula:

wikiContext.title: Chilled ground
wikiContext.summary: Chilled Ground is a detrimental ground effect that inflicts chill.
mechanics: Like regular chill, chilled ground reduces action speed, modifying the speed of the enemy's animations. Unless otherwise specified, chilled ground slows for 10%. Since version 3.9.0, the magnitude of chilled ground from map mods are 10%/20%/30% dependent on map tier. The actual magnitude of chill will be shown in the status icon, once the player character has stepped on the Chilled Ground and affected by it.

Chilled ground created by a player is affected by modifiers to the effect of cold and/or non-damaging ailments, including from the player's stats and support gems. Chilled ground never counts as chills inflicted by the player. It cannot apply chilled by you stats, cannot make the player count as having chilled recently and can chill regardless of stats that prevent the application of chill by the player, such as Elemental Focus or Secrets of Suffering.

wikiContext.title: Controlled Blaze Support
wikiContext.summary: Controlled Blaze is a support gem that causes melee attacks to have an increased chance to ignite and for each Ignite inflicted with the Skill recently, it deals less Damage but more Ignite Damage.
mechanics: Controlled Blaze will count all hits that have applied ignite, for each monster that received an ignite and any ignite that has been re-applied to an already ignited enemy.

Due to the fact that more and less modifiers are multiplicative, Controlled Blaze will provide less DPS at high number of ignites applied recently. Depending on the gem level, the number of ignites you need to inflict to reach its highest damage bonus is 12 or 13. This results in a "sweet spot" of 3 to 3.25 attacks per second (assuming no other targets); however, it is better to exceed this value to account for time not spent attacking while dodging/repositioning. That said, in general, you can be about 4 ignites off from the optimal range before you start experiencing a >5% ignite DPS loss.

wikiContext.title: Shrine
wikiContext.summary: Shrines are special objects that apply an effect to nearby monsters or cast spells at nearby players. Interacting them allows the player to temporarily steal their power for themselves. This mechanic is also referred to as Domination.
mechanics: Shrines can appear randomly in most areas. Shrines are often surrounded by a pack of monsters guarding it. Initially, shrines will only buff enemies and damage players. When touched, the shrine's effect is removed and given to the player for 45 seconds (20 seconds for Divine Shrines) in the form of a status effect. Shrine effects will either buff the player (but not their allies) or cast spells that damage enemies. A player can be affected by multiple different shrine effects.
Shrine effect duration and buff effect can be modified with certain items and passives.

wikiContext.title: Critical strike
wikiContext.summary: A critical strike is a type of hit that multiplies its damage by its critical strike multiplier.
mechanics: When a skill is used or triggers, it performs a critical strike roll. This roll ranges from 0 to 99.99, and determines the critical strike chance a hit must exceed to critically strike.

:For example: A player casts Arc and rolls a 12. When enemies are hit, those hits require a critical strike chance of 12.01% to become critical strikes. While hits from the same skill will usually have the same critical strike chance, resulting in all-or-nothing behaviour, conditional modifiers such as Assassin's Mark or For the Jugular can cause critical strike chance to vary between enemies or hits.

mechanics: Cruelty grants more damage over time with supported skills based on the damage of the hit compared to the target's maximum life. It lasts 4 seconds by default, and has a maximum effect of 40%. The maximum is unaffected by modifiers to Cruelty effect.

At gem level 20, The Cruelty buff provides 15.85% more damage over time to skills supported by Cruelty when the hit does 0.01% of the monster's ailment threshold and 40% more damage over time to skills supported by Cruelty when the hit does 3.2% of the monster's ailment threshold. Taking Shaper's 7 million ailment threshold as an example, a hit of 224k is needed to reach the maximum buff of 40%.

wikiContext.title: Destructive Link
wikiContext.summary: Destructive Link is a Link skill that targets an allied player to apply a buff which links you to them for a duration. While linked, they use your critical strike chance for main hand hits. If the target dies while linked, you will also die. This skill cannot be used by Totems, Traps, or Mines.
mechanics: This skill replaces the linked target's main hand critical strike chance with yours; this uses the value in the player's character sheet which is affected by modifiers to critical strike chance, not just the base critical strike chance of the weapon. Tecrod's Gaze, for example, will affect this value.

The critical strike chance of the linked target cannot be further modified through stats on the linked target. For example, a linked player with Marylene's Fallacy will not have their critical strike chance lowered by the item.

mechanics: Spend Energy Shield before Mana for Skill Mana Costs : allows paying mana costs by spending energy shield. * Unlike Blood Magic or Lifetap Support, this does not change mana costs into energy shield costs. The player still pays a mana cost, and can modify that cost with mana cost modifiers. * Energy shield recharge is not interrupted by energy shield spent to pay costs. Unless interrupted by damage to mana or energy shield, energy shield will continually recharge. * Energy shield can only be spent for mana costs. will still spend mana, Apep's Rage will still cause mana loss. * Has negative synergy with Arcane Surge Support, Inspiration Support, Sigil of Power, and other mechanics that require mana to be spent.

Energy Shield protects Mana instead of Life: allows energy shield to protect mana from damage * Damage may be taken to mana through % of Damage is taken from Mana before Life or similar modifiers (e.g. Mind of the Council). * Damage that bypasses energy shield, such as chaos damage, will still bypass energy shield. * Damage to energy shield or mana will interrupt energy shield recharge.

wikiContext.title: Conflux
wikiContext.summary: Confluxes are a family of non-stackable keyword buffs that make hits apply an elemental ailment, and allow all damage types to contribute to the magnitude of that ailment.
mechanics: A Conflux allows hits to inflict a specific ailment without requiring a chance stat (e.g. #% chance to Ignite) or a critical strike. Additionally, the ailment will be based on the total damage of the hit, from all combined damage types.

For example, when the player with Igniting Conflux deals a hit with base damage of the following types: * 200 Physical * 50 Fire * 100 Cold * 150 Chaos that hit will apply ignite with a DPS value based on the total 500 damage.

mechanics: Skills that have dealt a Critical Strike in the past 8 seconds deal 40% more Elemental Damage with Hits and Ailments: When a skill deals a critical strike, it gains more elemental damage for 8 seconds, limited to hits and ailments. * This damage bonus does not apply to the critical strike that caused Elemental Overload's effect to activate, only to hits while it is already active. * It does not apply to non-ailment damage over time such as Fire Trap's burning ground, even if it activates EO by critting. * This effect is not a buff or a skill effect; its duration cannot be affected by modifiers to skill effect duration or expiration rate (e.g. Temporal Chains).

Skills used by proxies such as totems, traps, or mines will activate Elemental Overload for the player's skill when they crit, which will then apply to all uses of that skill, including by those proxies. Minions are unaffected by Elemental Overload, even the skill that summoned them can crit (e.g. Absolution).

mechanics: At first glance the mod Nearby Enemies have 50% increased Fire and Cold Resistances may sound unhelpful; however, it also multiplies negative resistances.

For example, if a monster's Cold Resistance was lowered to -30% via sources such as Exposure, Frostbite, Void Beacon, and other methods, Eye of Malice's effect would cause that monster to have -45% instead. Note that this modifier affects the actual resistance (or tooltip resistance) of the monster; it does not scale on player side by how many -#% to monster resistances with any given method (i.e. the scaling is calculated on monster side). Conversely, a monster with 30% Cold Resistance after applying any player's aura/curse/other #% res effect, will have 45% Cold Resistance instead. Therefore, it is important to stack lots of sources of Resistance stripping to get the monster negative.

mechanics: Multiple Exposures of the same element do not stack; only the strongest Exposure per element applies. Exposures of different elements can apply to the same target.

Exposure debuffs inflicted by the player or their skills apply -10% to the affected resistance by default. This base value can be overridden by certain effects and skills: * Elemental Equilibrium: -25% for each element a hit didn't deal the damage type of * Scorching Ray: -25% to Fire Resistance * Frost Bomb: -15% to Cold Resistance * Wave of Conviction: -15% to the Elemental Resistance matching the highest damage taken

wikiContext.title: Flame Wall

mechanics: Casting a Flame Wall directly on an enemy will cause them to be inside its area, applying the primary debuff, and it will also count as them 'entering' the wall, applying the secondary debuff. Both debuffs can deal damage at the same time. Multiple copies of the same debuff cannot; only the highest dps primary and secondary debuffs will be active. The duration of the secondary debuff does not begin expiring until the enemy leaves Flame Wall's area.

wikiContext.title: Fortification
wikiContext.summary: Fortification is a stackable buff. Entities inherently have 1% less damage taken from hits per stack of Fortification. By default, it has a maximum of 20 stacks and lasts 6 seconds. The amount of stacks gained per hit depends on a combination of the hit's damage, the enemy's ailment threshold, and the enemy's rarity.
mechanics: When you hit an enemy with a fortifying hit, you will gain a variable number of stacks, based on the target's damage taken, that target's ailment threshold, and its rarity. The Fortification generation bonus against magic, rare, and unique monsters may cause you to generate more stacks against a map boss than a normal monster in the same map, despite the boss's higher ailment threshold. There is no minimum number of stacks; insufficient damage can cause a hit to grant 0 stacks, even with 100% chance to Fortify.

The fortification calculation ignores some forms of mitigation, for example against monsters in the Azurite Mine, Simulacrum, or monsters that have just been spawned by certain league mechanics. It does not ignore regular mitigation such as damage reduction (from armour).

mechanics: Shrines can appear randomly in most areas. Shrines are often surrounded by a pack of monsters guarding it. Initially, shrines will only buff enemies and damage players. Shrine effect duration and buff effect can be modified with certain items and passives.

wikiContext.title: Freeze
wikiContext.summary: Freeze (known in status as Frozen) is an elemental ailment associated with cold that causes affected targets to become frozen solid, preventing them from moving or using skills directly. Certain enemies cannot be fully slowed, but can still be considered frozen, which will result in them having significantly lower action speed.
mechanics: Hits that deal cold damage can inherently freeze; the chance for this to occur is dependent on chance to freeze. Critical strikes with cold damage inherently have a 100% chance to freeze. Other damage types are unable to cause or contribute to freeze by default, though certain stats can allow them to do so (e.g. Expedition's End, The Three Dragons).

Note that freeze and are separate ailments. A frozen enemy is not necessarily always chilled, though this is often the case (due to cold damage). For example, The Three Dragons can cause lightning damage to freeze an enemy, but the lightning damage cannot inherently chill., due to freeze being 100% less, nullifying these kinds of stats.

wikiContext.title: Grace Period
wikiContext.summary: Grace Period is a buff that prevents affected characters and minions from taking damage, as well as preventing monsters from targeting them. If the character performs any action (using a skill, moving, using a flask), the buff will be removed from them and their minions. This buff is granted to any character and their minions when they enter certain areas, upon which it will be granted for a duration specific to the area. It is impossible for monsters to be affected by this buff, or for players to obtain this buff through any alternative method. When an entity is affected by Grace Period, they are referred as being "in the Grace Period".
mechanics: While in the Grace Period: * Affected characters take no damage. * Affected minions take no damage. * Affected minions do not attack. * Monsters will not attack affected minions or players.

Some bosses have attacks with completely unavoidable damage for players that have recently entered the instance. An example is The Maven's attack on failing a Memory Game. If you have failed the Memory Game, logout or die, and reenter the instance, it is almost always advisable to stay in the Grace Period if you can see that her failed Memory Game skill is being used, as the damage is unavoidable.

wikiContext.title: Ignite
wikiContext.summary: Ignite is a damaging elemental ailment associated with fire that causes the affected target to take burning damage (fire damage over time).
mechanics: Hits ignite when they combine a chance to ignite with damage capable of igniting. This is normally limited to fire damage, but can include other types through effects like Stormfire, Shaper of Flames, Hexblast, or a Conflux buff. Damage over time effects such as Righteous Fire do not hit and therefore cannot inflict ignite. Critical strikes inherently have a 100% chance to ignite, though they still need damage capable of igniting; 0 DPS ignites are discarded.

The base duration of ignite is 4 seconds. Increasing the duration of the Ignite, either via Temporal Chains or the % increased Ignite duration modifier, causes the ignite to deal the same damage per second for a greater period of time. Ignite is not affected by skill effect duration.

wikiContext.title: Impale
wikiContext.summary: Impale is a mechanic that applies the Impaled debuff. Impaled enemies take reflected physical damage whenever they are hit, for a number of hits.
mechanics: The Impaled debuff records 10% of the physical damage of the hit that applies it. Each time the target is hit after that, by any source, the debuff deals that amount of reflected physical damage. Impale lasts for 5 hits by default, or 8 seconds. applied before the regular hit's on-hit effects. As reflected damage, the impale hit cannot stun or separately apply on-hit or when-hit effects. While the impale hit is technically dealt by the attacker (for the purpose of e.g. Southbound), impale is an effect on the enemy which causes reflection to them, not damage reflected by the attacker for effects like Crown of the Pale King. Impale is mitigated normally when the debuff actually deals damage. It cannot be evaded, dodged, suppressed, or blocked, but it can be affected by mechanics such as damage taken as, avoidance, damage reduction, and modifiers to damage taken, including reflect-specific modifiers. For example, Slayer's Bane of Legends will prevent taking impale damage.
Impale debuffs can remain on corpses when enemies are killed, and impale can be applied to enemies killed by a single impaling hit.

sources.license: Game data and artwork © Grinding Gear Games; RePoE source attribution retained

wikiContext.title: Infernal Blow
wikiContext.summary: Infernal Blow is a melee attack skill that converts 60% of Physical Damage to Fire Damage and applies a debuff to enemies. The debuff causes enemies to explode on death, dealing secondary damage. Additionally, if the debuff has charges, it deals attack area damage when an enemy gains 6 stacks, when the debuff expires, or when the enemy dies. This skill requires a sword, axe, mace, staff or unarmed.
mechanics: Damage conversion: Like all converted damage, the fire portion of Infernal Blow's damage will be modified by both fire damage increases and physical damage increases.

Uncharged debuff: At 0 charges, the debuff only causes enemies to explode on death, scaling with the affected enemy's maximum life. * The explosion deals fire area secondary damage and cannot be reflected. It does not use your weapon, nor does it scale with modifiers to attack or melee damage. It can be scaled by generic modifiers and Elemental Damage with Attack Skills. Like other corpse explosions, it ignores life bonuses from partying and atlas keystones like Wellspring of Creation. The corpse explosion will generally prevent on-death effects, such as porcupine spines, as well as prevent enemy necromancers from resurrecting the corpses, like other explode-on-death effects.

wikiContext.title: Infernal Cry
wikiContext.summary: Infernal Cry is a warcry skill gem that taunts nearby enemies, debuffs enemies to explode on death, buffs the user and allies to gain extra fire damage based on their physical damage, and exerts a number of subsequent attacks, causing those attacks to trigger the Combust attack.
mechanics: Infernal Cry gem has two parts: Infernal Cry and Combust. These are distinct skills and do not share all their stats. Infernal Cry's Damage cannot be Reflected only applies to its debuff's explosion, not hits by Combust. Similarly, Combust's 60% of Physical Damage Converted to Fire Damage will not affect physical damage added to Infernal Cry's debuff explosion.
Both the explosion and Combust can be affected by support gems linked to Infernal Cry.

wikiContext.title: Inspired Learning
wikiContext.summary: Inspired Learning is a unique Crimson Jewel.
mechanics: Upon killing a rare monster, the character gains one of its modifiers for the next 20 seconds. As a special exception, this item's on-kill effect works with minions and proxies. Note that although when capturing a beast, the beast will drop loot, but it does not count as killing.

This jewel can be considered a low-power version of the similar stat on Headhunter, which provides the ability to gain all monster modifiers from a slain rare enemy. Because stolen modifiers cannot stack, there is no benefit to combining Inspired Learning with Headhunter; it will only reduce the duration of one stolen modifier from 60 seconds to 20.

mechanics: Without other items and passive skills, the maximum stack of Intensity is 3. An Intensity stack is lost once every 0.5 seconds while moving.

Spending a certain amount of life grants the Lifetap buff, which allows skills supported by Lifetap to deal more damage.
mechanics: Supported Skills Cost Life instead of Mana: * This is not a conversion mechanic: the cost will no longer be affected by modifiers specific for mana costs. * Additional base mana costs (e.g. Divine Blessing Support, Inverted Elreon's) do add to life cost.

Gain Lifetap after Spending a total of # Life with a Supported Skill: * The buff grants 20% increased Life Recovery from Flasks and has a duration of 4 seconds. * Because the buff has a duration, supported skills will become supportable by supports like Less Duration Support and Swift Affliction Support. This does not add a duration gem tag; supported skills will not be affected by modifiers like +# to Level of Socketed Duration Gems. * The player may choose to use a lower level Lifetap gem to gain the buff after less life spent.

wikiContext.title: Leech
wikiContext.summary: Leech recovers an amount of life, mana, or energy shield over time, relative to the damage inflicted on an enemy. Leech is based on the damage taken by the enemy, not the amount of life removed.
mechanics: There are a few notable ways to affect leech: * A skill supported by the Life Leech, Mana Leech, or Energy Leech Support grants leech of their respective types. * Bone Barrier, The Baron, Machina Mitts, Totem Mastery and Trolltimber Spire allow other entities to leech life for you. * Brutal Fervour, , Immortal Ambition, Offering to the Serpent, Soul Drinker and Essentia Sanguis allow leech instances to continue even if the character's unreserved life (or energy shield) is filled. Petrified Blood achieves a similar effect by preventing recovery above low life. * Players can prevent enemies from leeching life from them by equipping Sin Trek or allocating Bloodless.

No stat currently exists to modify the base rate of a leech instance. The maximum recovery may be modified through , which in turn modifies maximum duration. For example, a 100% increase from Brutal Fervour will result in a maximum recovery per life leech of 20%, recovered at a rate of 2% per second for 10 seconds.

wikiContext.title: One Step Ahead
wikiContext.summary: One Step Ahead is a notable Ascendancy passive skill for the Trickster that sets the user's action speed minimum to 90% and nearby monsters' maximum action speed to 90%.
mechanics: This passive affects modifiers to action speed, such as Tailwind and Chill. Effects that can set the user's action speed to 0% such as Freeze and Petrify will have its effects greatly mitigated, allowing to benefit from self-freeze mechanics or Replica Rumi's Concoction at a much lower downside. It also mitigates the action speed reduction of Temporal Chains without affecting the slower expiration rate of various effects, making it useful for self-curse builds.
It does not affect Movement Speed slows like Maim and Hinder.

wikiContext.title: Pacify
wikiContext.summary: This skill is granted by The Queller of Minds, and by Bog Shaman's .
mechanics: Pacify targets enemies in an area, having no effect initially but causes affected enemies to deal no damage after 60% of the curse's duration has expired. Pacify does not prevent on-hit effects, and has no effect on mechanics that instantly kill the player or arena hazards like the Drowning orbs in Absence of Symmetry and Harmony, or Sirus' Deatomization Storm. Casting Pacify on a target already affected by Pacify will reset the curse's duration.

Increasing curse duration will lengthen the period of damage nullification, but also increases the time required to reach that effect; conversely, reducing curse duration will make the effect apply faster but have a smaller window of nullification. Pacify does not directly scale with curse effect, but 100% reduced curse effect will prevent the damage nullification.

wikiContext.title: Plague Bearer
wikiContext.summary: Plague Bearer is a chaos spell skill that grants the user a buff that can be toggled between Incubating or Infecting. While Incubating, the buff causes the user to deal less poison damage, and charges Plague Value based on inflicted poisons. While Infecting, the buff depletes its Plague Value to deal chaos damage over time to nearby enemies.
mechanics: The gem's advanced description specifies (The Expected Damage of Poison is its Damage per second multiplied by its Duration). This is based on the poison's base DPS and duration, and is not affected by the defender's stats such as resistances. Poisoning through The Golden Rule's reflection also charges Plague Bearer, effectively doubling Plague Value gain.

Plague Bearer inflicts its Infecting debuff in an area around the player, similar to Righteous Fire. This damage cannot be further scaled by the user's offensive stats. Its damage is mitigated normally by the enemy through e.g. resistance and damage taken modifiers (including Delirium), and accordingly can be scaled through debuffs like Despair, , or . Its damage is not considered poison.

wikiContext.title: Tormented spirit
wikiContext.summary: Tormented Spirits are a special type of undead monster. Once spotted, these apparitions of dead criminals flee from the player with their ill-gotten gains. When a tormented spirit touch another monster, it imbues them a with buff that increases their danger, but also their reward. When a tormented spirit touches a Rare or Unique monster, it possesses it and makes them even more powerful, but also makes them more rewarding. This mechanic is also referred to as Torment.
mechanics: Tormented spirits are Unique monsters that can be randomly found throughout acts and maps. Tormented spirits are unable to attack directly. Once a player gets within range, it will attempt to flee from the player while also attempting to pass through other monsters along the way, stopping every few seconds.

Any Normal and Magic monsters that the spirit passes through receive a "Touch" modifier based on the spirit type. If the tormented spirit touches a Rare or Unique monster, it will go inside that monster and possess it, despawning itself and giving the monster a "Grip" modifier. Tormented spirits cannot affect other tormented spirits. If a tormented spirit stays alive long enough without possessing anything it will eventually despawn itself, leaving no items. Certain effects can cause monsters to spawn in with a Touch or Grip modifier already applied.

wikiContext.title: Proximity Shield
wikiContext.summary: ]] Proximity Shield is a defensive area of effect ability used by a monster, taking the form of a dome with the user at its centre. The user and their allies within the shielded area are protected from direct damage from enemies outside the shield.
mechanics: A Proximity Shield removes the damage of hits coming from enemies outside the shield. It does not physically obstruct objects or projectiles like a Frost Wall; it simply checks the locations of the entity that hit and the entity that was hit. Removing all hit damage also prevents effects that require non-zero damage, such as ailments. Proximity shield does not prevent hits entirely, nor does it prevent non-ailment debuffs applied by hits, including damage over time debuffs such as Essence Drain or Corrupting Fever.

To counter proximity shield monsters, the player can: * enter the shield * inflict non-ailment damage over time * apply damaging ailments without a direct hit, e.g. proliferation * make their minions or proxies enter the shield, or create them directly inside it

wikiContext.title: Radiant Faith
wikiContext.summary: Radiant Faith is a notable Ascendancy passive skill for the Guardian that grants the Radiant Faith buff, which grants increased energy shield and additional armour relative to the amount of mana you've reserved to you and nearby allies.
mechanics: Because Radiant Faith is classified as an aura buff and not an aura skill / aura skill gem, mods such as #% increased effect of Non-Curse Auras from your Skills does not increase the amount of Armour and Energy Shield granted from this ascendancy passive skill. However, those receiving the buff can increase the amounts received by their own Increased Armour and Increased Energy Shield stats.

Note, that while the wording is similar to the Hierophant's Sanctuary of Thought, the mechanics are quite different. Sanctuary of Thought functions as a conversion so Increased Maximum Mana and Increased Maximum Energy Shield mods stack with each other additively. Radiant Faith grants the percentage of your actual mana as base energy shield, so Increased Maximum Mana and Increased Maximum Energy Shield effectively stack multiplicatively with each other, which allows for extreme stacking of energy shield with proper gear.

more Damage per affected Ally: This modifier counts the number of allies buffed by the warcry. wikiContext.title: Shrine

mechanics: Shrines can appear randomly in most areas. Shrines are often surrounded by a pack of monsters guarding it. Initially, shrines will only buff enemies and damage players. Shrine effect duration and buff effect can be modified with certain items and passives.

entries.name: Righteous Fire
entries.definition: You take burning damage, deal burning damage to those around you, and have increased spell damage.

sources.license: Game data and artwork © Grinding Gear Games; RePoE source attribution retained

wikiContext.title: Righteous Fire
wikiContext.summary: Righteous Fire is a spell that applies a buff to the player, granting more spell damage, but also applying a potent burning effect that scales with the user's maximum life and energy shield to both the user and nearby enemies.
mechanics: Damage over time effect: While the Righteous Fire buff is active, the player and surrounding enemies will take fire damage over time. * The self-damage can be mitigated like regular fire damage over time: it can be shifted (e.g. Divine Flesh), resisted, reduced by elemental damage reduction (e.g. endurance charges, Eternal Damnation), or modified as damage taken (e.g. Soul of Arakaali). * Damage can be taken by resources like energy shield, life, or mana (e.g. with Mind over Matter), and can be sustained with enough recovery for these resources, such as regeneration. * Damage over time does not hit, and accordingly Righteous Fire's self-damage cannot be blocked, suppressed, or reflected. It also cannot be recouped or contribute to Cast when Damage Taken. * The self-damage does not count as being ignited.

Stopping Righteous Fire: Righteous Fire's buff and burning effect will apply until the player reaches 1 life, at which point the buff is removed. The effect can be ended prematurely by any effect which removes burning, such as flasks with a Removes Burning on use affix. Unsocketing the gem out of its socket will remove the skill effect, but will not stop the burning effect. *Chaos Inoculation: Righteous Fire cannot be activated if Chaos Inoculation is allocated, as the buff is removed immediately when the player is on 1 life (which is all the time with Chaos Inoculation).

wikiContext.title: Ruin
wikiContext.summary: Ruin is a debuff primarily found in Ultimatum encounters, as well as a modifier for Valdo's Maps. Accumulating 7 stacks of Ruin will cause the party to fail the Ultimatum encounter, and kick players out to the main area of the map if they were currently in the Trialmaster's arena. In Valdo's Maps, failing will prevent the reward chest from spawning.
mechanics: Enemy attacks that apply Ruin are subject to a shared cooldown between applications, preventing additional stacks from being applied until a short delay has passed, regardless of the number of sources.

Evasion, spell dodge, hit avoidance, and block (with or without damage taken from block e.g. ) prevent Ruin from being applied. Though the melee attacks of shades spawned by Stalking Ruin cannot be Evaded.

mechanics: Rupture is a dynamic debuff: an enemy starts taking more damage from all their bleeds when they become Ruptured, and cease to do so when Rupture expires. Similarly, an enemy that becomes Ruptured will have the timers on their bleeding debuffs speed up, and return to normal speed if Rupture is removed.

Unlike Bleeding you inflict deals Damage #% faster, Rupture does not affect the base DPS and base duration values of bleeding debuffs. Due to applying to different things at different times, the overall effect on damage dealt is effectively multiplicative.

mechanics: A Conflux allows hits to inflict a specific ailment without requiring a chance stat (e.g. #% chance to Ignite) or a critical strike. Additionally, the ailment will be based on the total damage of the hit, from all combined damage types.

wikiContext.summary: Scorch is an Elemental Ailment associated with fire that causes the affected target to have their Elemental Resistances lowered by up to 30%, based on the Fire Damage of the Hit, for 4 seconds.
mechanics: where D is the fire damage dealt, T is the enemy's ailment threshold, and M is the sum of the attacker's increases to the effect of scorch/non-damaging ailments (normally 0%). Usually the ailment threshold is equal to the monster's full life, except some end-game bosses such as The Shaper. To achieve the maximum magnitude , the player character needed to deal damage equal to (0.6^2.5)*100% of the ailment threshold, which roughly equal to 28% of the ailment threshold, or 28% life for most monsters. These calculations do not account for increases to ailment effect.
Scorched with a base effect lower than 2% is discarded. Scorched inflicted through means other than hit damage has a base effect of 10%.

wikiContext.title: Scourge Arrow
wikiContext.summary: Scourge Arrow is a channelling bow attack skill. Channelling the skill charges up an arrow that creates spore pods as the arrow travels when released. The pods explode to fire thorn arrows around them. The arrow and pods deal physical damage converted to chaos damage.
mechanics: Additional arrows (from support gems and items like Death's Harp) apply to the primary arrow, instead of the thorn arrows. Additional arrows cause spore pods to distribute evenly among each primary arrow, rather than in a line from player. Having more arrows than pods will not cause additional pods to spawn. Therefore at 5 stages Scourge Arrow will spawn 5 pods — if the player has 6 total arrows (5 additional) one of the arrows will not spawn a pod.

The distance between each spore pod can be increased by releasing the channel while mouse cursor is near the edge of your screen. With 4 additional arrows, the spore pods spawn in a cluster near your mouse cursor.

Its default value is 15%, with shocked ground from map mods applying 20%, 35%, or 50% in white, yellow, or red maps respectively. The magnitude of the map mod may further scale with #% increased effect of Modifiers on non-unique Maps.

When created by the character, shock effect will scale with the player's #% increased effect of ailments modifiers. Shocks from shocked ground are not attributed to the creator of the shocked ground; it does not interact with effects that care about Shocked by you, but conversely it can shock while you have the Cannot Shock stat.

wikiContext.title: Conflux
wikiContext.summary: Confluxes are a family of non-stackable keyword buffs that make hits apply an elemental ailment, and allow all damage types to contribute to the magnitude of that ailment.
mechanics: A Conflux allows hits to inflict a specific ailment without requiring a chance stat (e.g. #% chance to Ignite) or a critical strike. Additionally, the ailment will be based on the total damage of the hit, from all combined damage types.

For example, when the player with Igniting Conflux deals a hit with base damage of the following types: * 200 Physical * 50 Fire * 100 Cold * 150 Chaos that hit will apply ignite with a DPS value based on the total 500 damage.

wikiContext.title: Shrine
wikiContext.summary: Shrines are special objects that apply an effect to nearby monsters or cast spells at nearby players. Interacting them allows the player to temporarily steal their power for themselves. This mechanic is also referred to as Domination.
mechanics: Shrines can appear randomly in most areas. Shrines are often surrounded by a pack of monsters guarding it. Initially, shrines will only buff enemies and damage players. When touched, the shrine's effect is removed and given to the player for 45 seconds (20 seconds for Divine Shrines) in the form of a status effect. Shrine effects will either buff the player (but not their allies) or cast spells that damage enemies. A player can be affected by multiple different shrine effects.
Shrine effect duration and buff effect can be modified with certain items and passives.

mechanics: Maximum Active Brands: All brands share a limit of three (3) active brand limit. This can be split between the two brand skills (2-1) or all of one type. Passive skills can increase the number of active brands that are allowed to be active at a time.

Maximum Brand Attachment: By default, you may only have one brand of any kind attached to a single target at any time. Taking the Keystone Runebinder allows you to place a second brand on a single target. Like the Active Brand limit these brands may either be split (1-1) or both the same type of brand.

wikiContext.title: Shrine
wikiContext.summary: Shrines are special objects that apply an effect to nearby monsters or cast spells at nearby players. Interacting them allows the player to temporarily steal their power for themselves. This mechanic is also referred to as Domination.
mechanics: Shrines can appear randomly in most areas. Shrines are often surrounded by a pack of monsters guarding it. Initially, shrines will only buff enemies and damage players. When touched, the shrine's effect is removed and given to the player for 45 seconds (20 seconds for Divine Shrines) in the form of a status effect. Shrine effects will either buff the player (but not their allies) or cast spells that damage enemies. A player can be affected by multiple different shrine effects.
Shrine effect duration and buff effect can be modified with certain items and passives.

wikiContext.title: Tincture
wikiContext.summary: A tincture is an item that can be equipped in a flask slot and activated to enhance the user's melee weapons with special bonuses. While active, they inflict Mana Burn on the user, causing mana loss over time at an accelerating rate, and will automatically deactivate when you reach 0 mana. By default, you can only have one tincture active at a time.
mechanics: Upon using a tincture, it activates the tincture, granting its effects. While a tincture is active, you gain stacks of Mana Burn over time. Mana Burn causes you to lose 1% of your maximum Mana per stack per second. A stack of Mana Burn will always drain a minimum of 1 mana. Tinctures deactivate when manually deactivated or when you reach 0 mana. Once a tincture is deactivated, it procs a cooldown on all tinctures, preventing you from activating any tincture for the duration. The rate at which you gain Mana Burn and the duration of the cooldown depends on the tincture base type and associated stats and modifiers.

:Bloodsoaked Blade will cause Mana Burn and all associated effects to instead apply Weeping Wounds, which is identical to Mana Burn except that it drains 1% of maximum life per stack per second instead.

wikiContext.title: Herald of Agony
wikiContext.summary: Herald of Agony is a herald skill gem. When activated it reserves mana and grants a buff that gives a chance to inflict poison on enemies. Whenever the user poisons an enemy, it grants Virulence and summons an Agony Crawler minion, which becomes stronger with more stacks of Virulence.
mechanics: The regular maximum is 40 stacks, which can be raised with the Cluster Jewel notable passive Pure Agony, additional quality on the gem gained via methods such as Enhance or Ashes of the Stars, and from the Herald's Scourge node.

Virulence decays at an accelerating rate based on the number of stacks you have. Stacks have a base duration rate of 533ms, minus 12.5ms per stack of Virulence capping out at a minimum duration of 33ms (1 server tick) at 40+ stacks. In other words, poison must be inflicted at a rate of 30 stacks per second to sustain maximum Virulence higher than 40.

wikiContext.title: Winter Orb
wikiContext.summary: Winter Orb is a channelling spell skill. Channelling the skill charges up an orb, which fires icy projectiles that deal cold damage in an area of effect where they land.
mechanics: Projectiles from Winter Orb don't directly collide with enemies, and accordingly cannot split, pierce, fork, chain, or return. Its projectiles benefit from both area damage and projectile damage modifiers.
The first stage does not gain projectile frequency. Therefore 8 stages gives (7 X 20) = 140% increased projectile frequency. The plus 2 maximum stages at 20% quality adds 40% projectile frequency.

wikiContext.title: Zealot's Oath
wikiContext.summary: Zealot's Oath is a keystone passive skill that applies life regeneration to energy shield instead of life.
mechanics: Percentage and flat life regeneration becomes percentage and flat ES regeneration, including from outside sources such as allied Consecrated Ground. Percentage ES regeneration is based on maximum ES. This is not a conversion mechanic. ES regeneration gained through Zealot's Oath will only scale with ES Recovery Rate, not Life Recovery Rate or Life Regeneration Rate.
Non-regeneration forms of life recovery such as recoup, leech, or life flasks are unaffected by Zealot's Oath.

mechanics: The buff (displayed as flask effect) granted from this flask has the following effect: Last Breath recovers an amount of life per second based on mana cost.
